subject: Sable Therapeutics — throughput & latency safety evaluation for Dedicated commit
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@sabletx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sable Dedicated sizing proposal — initial throughput & headroom ask

Hi Asha,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, I ran a quick sizing sketch for the Dedicated commit you asked about. I want to surface the key numbers and proposed next steps so Procurement and your infra team have something to react to.

Summary (high level):
- Target p95 latency: 300ms for text-generation flows (single-turn prompts, 1–2k tokens).
- Expected steady-state traffic: 180k tokens/sec during business hours (US), with 3x short-term bursts up to ~540k tokens/sec for 10–20m windows (peak events).
- Model baseline: open Llama-2 style 13B quantized variant (we used Redwood-13B-q4) — reserve path available to an ensemble of a 13B + 7B fallback.

Initial recommendation: Reserve a 32-GPU slab (A100-equivalent) with 20% headroom to meet SLO during peaks and allow KV-prefetch caching for common prefixes. This maps to our estimated token capacity of ~600k tokens/sec sustained at p95 under the workload mix we discussed.

I attached the full workbook with assumptions and per-GPU tokens/sec math (sable_capacity_model_v1.xlsx). Can you confirm:
1) Is the 3x burst multiple accurate for planning?
2) Are there quiet hours where traffic drops by >70% (we can plan autoscale windows)?

If Procurement wants, we can convert the sketch into a formal mutual action plan and a pilot commit that buys a smaller slab first.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sable_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Date: 2027-12-02T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sable Dedicated sizing proposal — initial throughput & headroom ask

Kimberly — thanks for the quick write-up and the workbook. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 3x burst figure is reasonable for launches and clinical-alert windows; for routine marketing events it's closer to 1.8–2x.
- Quiet hours: we do see ~80% drop overnight (0200–0600 PT) and a secondary trough on weekends (~65% down).
- We plan to start with a single model (13B-ish) for release 1, then incrementally add a reranker/fallback for rare queries.

Procurement would like a clearer mapping from tokens/sec to committed seats and an estimated month-to-month spend delta between the 32-GPU slab vs a 16-GPU pilot. Can Ben or Priyom help with a p95-cost vs capacity curve?

Also looping Ethan for infra constraints (network/storage) — Ethan, any compatibility concerns on our end?

—Asha
Senior Product Manager, Sable Therapeutics

On Thu, Dec 2, 2027 at 10:03 AM Asha Patel <asha@sabletx.com> wrote:
> The 3x burst figure is reasonable for launches ...

Asha — quick reply with the engineering view and a simple mapping. End-to-end p95 numbers depend heavily on: model sequence length distribution, batching tolerance, and whether you can accept slight latency percentiles tradeoffs during the 10–20m bursts. With the assumptions Kimberly used (mean seq len 600 tokens, batching window 8–12ms), our measured per-GPU steady tokens/sec for Redwood-13B-q4 is ~18k tokens/sec at p95 in the lab.

Mapping:
- 16 GPUs -> ~288k tokens/sec steady (p95).
- 24 GPUs -> ~432k tokens/sec steady (p95).
- 32 GPUs -> ~576k tokens/sec steady (p95) (matches Kimberlys headroom note).

Burst handling: with aggressive KV caching + short pre-warm, the system can absorb ~2x instantaneous bursts without degrading p95 beyond 25%. For sustained 3x bursts we recommend either: a) temporary burst credits (reserved spare GPUs) or b) a short-term autoscale to dedicated burst capacity.

I'll attach a condensed p95 vs GPUs table in the workbook.

—Ben
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@sabletx.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-03T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sable Dedicated sizing proposal — initial throughput & headroom ask

Thanks — adding the operational mapping and a short-term phasing option.

Operational assumptions (for the workbook):
- Model: Redwood-13B-q4. Sequence length mix: 60% short (<256), 35% medium (256–1024), 5% long (>1024).
- Cache hit rate target: 12% prefix hit (typical for Sable-like clinical dialogs).
- Expected average token output per request: 180 tokens.

Phasing proposal (min friction pilot -> commit):
1) Pilot: 12 GPUs reserved (pilot slab) for 6 weeks to validate traffic profile and cold-start behavior. Estimated steady capacity ~216k tokens/sec (p95). Cost delta vs no commit: pilot credit applied, pricing in workbook.
2) Scale to 24 GPUs month 2 for holiday/launch window testing (covers ~432k tps p95).
3) Commit to 32 GPUs post-launch if observed peak >400k sustained for >48h in telemetry.

Attachment: sable_capacity_model_v1.xlsx — sheet 'phase_map' shows monthly cost vs estimated p95 headroom.

Operational notes: we recommend enabling prefix/KV cache tiering and setting a conservative batch target initially to avoid tail amplification. We'll instrument a prompt-set health monitor to watch for quality regressions when quantization interacts with caching.

—Priyom
Principal Product Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick infra note from Sable side:
- Network: we can expose a cross-account VPC peering and provide private endpoints; egress policies are controlled by our security team.
- Storage: we have NFS-backed checkpoints and are OK with Redwood's KV caching if keys stay ephemeral and encrypted-at-rest.
- SLA ask: our legal team will push for a 99.9% uptime SLA and a 200ms p95 target for critical endpoints — the latter is tighter than the 300ms you proposed.

If 200ms p95 is required, can you show a comparison table (tokens/sec per GPU at p95=200ms) so we can feed it to Legal/Engineering for tradeoffs?

—Ethan

- Procurement (Sable): we'll draft a pilot MSA and a mutual action plan. If the SLA negotiation is going to require 200ms at p95 we should set expectations that the pilot will prove viability before a 32-GPU commit.
- Internal ops: Jordan, please prepare a canary runbook for the pilot (routing, fallback to hosted API, and alert thresholds).

I'll send a DocuSign link for an initial pilot statement of work once we have the 200ms table.
